<r>Ant.</r> Deum, qui suos Mártýres ætérnis corónis decorávit, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum, qui suos Mártýres ætérnis corónis decorávit, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum, qui suos Mártýres ætérnis corónis decorávit, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum, qui suos Mártýres ætérnis corónis decorávit, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum, qui suos Mártýres ætérnis corónis decorávit, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.

b.ca346c5fb1:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>H</c>æresum surgunt nova monstra: crescit
Militum Christi pietas et ardor,
Scútaque invíctæ fidei tenéntes,
Fórtiter instant.

<h>T</h>u, Deus, clamant, hómini parásti
Cælicum panem, solidáque in arce,
Christe, tu Petro fidei dedísti
Esse Magistrum.

<h>I</h>am phalanx pergit generósa morti
Obviam; Iesum vocat hic, Mariám
Alter implórat, moriénte Matrem
Ore salútans.

<h>S</h>ic diem fortes óbeunt suprémum,
Hostis insáni fera vis triúmphat,
Membra spargúntur temeráta, terram
Sanguis inúndat.

<h>S</h>it Patri virtus, honor et potéstas,
Fílio sit laus párilis per ævum,
Flámini sancto résonent perénni
Cántica voce.
Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Sapiéntiæ
<r>Sap 3:1-8</r>
<n>1</n> Iustórum ánimæ in manu Dei sunt, et non tanget illos torméntum mortis.
<n>2</n> Visi sunt óculis insipiéntium mori, et æstimáta est afflíctio éxitus illórum,
<n>3</n> Et quod a nobis est iter extermínium; illi autem sunt in pace;
<n>4</n> Et si coram homínibus torménta passi sunt, spes illórum immortalitáte plena est.
<n>5</n> In paucis vexáti in multis bene disponéntur, quóniam Deus tentávit eos et invénit illos dignos se.
<n>6</n> Tamquam aurum in fornáce probávit illos, et quasi holocáusti hóstiam accépit illos, et in témpore erit respéctus illórum.
<n>7</n> Fulgébunt iusti et tamquam scintíllæ in arundinéto discúrrent;
<n>8</n> Iudicábunt natiónes et dominabúntur pópulis, et regnábit Dóminus illórum in perpétuum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Abstérget Deus omnem lácrimam ab óculis Sanctórum: et iam non erit ámplius neque luctus, neque clamor, sed nec ullus dolor:
* Quóniam prióra transiérunt.
<r>℣.</r> Non esúrient, neque sítient ámplius, neque cadet super illos sol, neque ullus æstus.
<r>℟.</r> Quóniam prióra transiérunt.
b.3bf0522b65:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May His blessing be upon us who doth live and reign for ever.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Wisdom
<r>Wis 3:1-8</r>
<n>1</n> But the souls of the just are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them.
<n>2</n> In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure was taken for misery:
<n>3</n> And their going away from us, for utter destruction: but they are in peace.
<n>4</n> And though in the sight of men they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality.
<n>5</n> Afflicted in few things, in many they shall be well rewarded: because God hath tried them, and found them worthy of himself.
<n>6</n> As gold in the furnace he hath proved them, and as a victim of a holocaust he hath received them, and in time there shall be respect had to them.
<n>7</n> The just shall shine, and shall run to and fro like sparks among the reeds.
<n>8</n> They shall judge nations, and rule over people, and their Lord shall reign for ever.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> God shall wipe away all tears from the eyes of His Saints, and there shall be no more sorrow, there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain;
* For the former things are passed away.
<r>℣.</r> They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more, neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat.
<r>℟.</r> For the former things are passed away.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
De libro Sapiéntiæ
<r>Sap 5:1-7; 14-17</r>
<n>1</n> Tunc stabunt iusti in magna constántia advérsus eos qui se angustiavérunt, et qui abstulérunt labóres eórum.
<n>2</n> Vidéntes turbabúntur timóre horríbili, et mirabúntur in subitatióne insperátæ salútis:
<n>3</n> Dicéntes intra se, pœniténtiam agéntes, et præ angústia spíritus geméntes: Hi sunt quos habúimus aliquándo in derísum, et in similitúdinem impropérii.
<n>4</n> Nos insensáti, vitam illórum æstimabámus insániam, et finem illórum sine honóre.
<n>5</n> Ecce quómodo computáti sunt inter fílios Dei, et inter sanctos sors illórum est.
<n>6</n> Ergo errávimus a via veritátis, et iustítiæ lumen non luxit nobis, et sol intelligéntiæ non est ortus nobis.
<n>7</n> Lassáti sumus in via iniquitátis et perditiónis, et ambulávimus vias diffíciles: viam autem Dómini ignorávimus.
<n>14</n> Tália dixérunt in inférno hi qui peccavérunt.
<n>15</n> Quóniam spes ímpii tamquam lanúgo est quæ a vento tóllitur, et tamquam spuma grácilis quæ a procélla dispérgitur, et tamquam fumus qui a vento diffúsus est, et tamquam memória hóspitis uníus diéi prætereúntis.
<n>16</n> Iusti autem in perpétuum vivent, et apud Dóminum est merces eórum, et cogitátio illórum apud Altíssimum.
<n>17</n> Ideo accípient regnum decóris, et diadéma speciéi de manu Dómini: quóniam déxtera sua teget eos, et bráchio sancto suo deféndet illos.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Viri sancti gloriósum sánguinem fudérunt pro Dómino, amavérunt Christum in vita sua, imitáti sunt eum in morte sua:
* Et ídeo corónas triumpháles meruérunt.
<r>℣.</r> Unus spíritus, et una fides erat in eis.
<r>℟.</r> Et ídeo corónas triumpháles meruérunt.

<h>Reading 2</h>
From the Book of Wisdom
<r>Sap 5:1-7; 14-17</r>
<n>1</n> Tunc the just shall stand with great constancy against those that have afflicted them, and taken away their labours.
<n>2</n> These seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the suddenness of their unexpected salvation.
<n>3</n> Saying within themselves, repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit: These are they, whom we had some time in derision, and for a parable of reproach.
<n>4</n> We fools esteemed their life madness, and their end without honour.
<n>5</n> Behold how they are numbered among the children of God, and their lot is among the saints.
<n>6</n> Therefore we have erred from the way of truth, and the light of justice hath not shined unto us, and the sun of understanding hath not risen upon us.
<n>7</n> We wearied ourselves in the way of iniquity and destruction, and have walked through hard ways, but the way of the Lord we have not known.
<n>14</n> Such things as these the sinners said in hell:
<n>15</n> Quóniam spes ímpii tamquam lanúgo est quæ a vento tóllitur, et tamquam spuma grácilis quæ a procélla dispérgitur, et tamquam fumus qui a vento diffúsus est, et tamquam memória hóspitis uníus diéi prætereúntis.
<n>16</n> But the just shall live for evermore: and their reward is with the Lord, and the care of them with the most High.
<n>17</n> Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty at the hand of the Lord: for with his right hand he will cover them, and with his holy arm he will defend them.

<c>J</c>uly 10th 2027, the 6th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, under Publius, Prefect of the City, in the time of the Emperor Antonine, seven holy Brethren, the sons of the holy martyr Felicity. Their names were Januarius, Felix, Philip, Silvanus, Alexander, Vitalis, and Martial. Januarius was first beaten with rods and starved, but in the end hided to death with scourges loaded with lead. Felix and Philip were beaten to death with clubs. Silvanus was killed by being cast over a steep place. Alexander, Vitalis, and Martial were beheaded.
<h>A</h>lso at Rome, the holy sisters Rufina and Secunda, both Virgins and both martyrs. In the persecution under the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus they were both tortured and then beheaded, and so passed to heaven. <h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Januarius, Marinus, Nabor, and Felix, who were all beheaded.
<h>A</h>t Nicopolis, in Armenia, the holy martyrs Leontius, Maurice, Daniel, and their Companions, who were put to diverse and dreadful torments under the Emperor Licinius, and the President Lysias, and at length were cast into the fire, and so finished the course of their testimony.
<h>I</h>n Pisidia, the holy martyrs Bianor and Sylvanus, who suffered most cruel torments for Christ's name's sake, and then were beheaded, and so received their crowns, [fourth century.]
<h>A</h>t Iconium, the holy martyr Apollonius, who finished his illustrious testimony upon the Cross, [fourth century.]
<h>A</h>t Gent [in Flanders], the holy Virgin Amelberga, [in the year 772. She was a nun in the Abbey of Munsterbilzen, in the Diocese of Liège. She died at the age of 31.]
